articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a nuclear payload of 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year because apparently browsers are the new Wild West.

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' Linux flaw makes CopyFail look quaint—public root exploit with no patches and a broken disclosure embargo. When responsible disclosure becomes irresponsible chaos, admins get the privilege of panicking.

articles.title: cPanel, WHM Release Fixes for Three New Vulnerabilities — Patch Now
articles.summary: Ollama's out-of-bounds read vulnerability lets remote attackers slurp entire process memory from 300,000+ servers globally. Because nothing says 'AI security' like leaking your brain directly to adversaries.

articles.title: A manual pentest costs 50,000 dollars. Intruder built an AI that does it in minutes.
articles.summary: The 90-day disclosure window is officially dead—LLMs compressed both bug finding and exploit development to near-zero timelines. The responsible disclosure social contract just got steamrolled by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: U.S. Fuel Exports Hit Record High as Hormuz Crisis Reshapes Global Energy Flows
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos AI discovered thousands of zero-days across major OS and browsers, prompting Fed chair emergency calls to bank CEOs. When your AI becomes too good at breaking everything, even the money people start sweating.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas learning platform got pwned during finals week by cybercriminals who defaced login pages with ransom demands. Nothing says 'educational disruption' like holding millions of students' coursework hostage.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military hackers are mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers because apparently every IoT device is now a state-sponsored espionage gateway. Your office WiFi router: now with 100% more GRU.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta abandons Instagram end-to-end encryption push, reverting DMs to plaintext after years of privacy promises. Zuckcorp wants full visibility into your chats again because surveillance capitalism never sleeps.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches—but only when convenient. Peak government hypocrisy: transparency for thee, opacity for me.

articles.title: Canvas Got Hacked During Finals Week and Students Are Freaking Out
articles.summary: NVIDIA confirms GeForce NOW data breach affecting Armenian users because even gaming platforms aren't safe from data harvesting operations. Your cloud gaming stats: now with complementary identity exposure.
